overview.heading: How the YouTube Thumbnail Maker works
paragraphs: Enter the words you want on the thumbnail, describe the video in a sentence or two and pick a style. If you upload a photo of yourself or the product, PiCraft makes it the focal point while keeping the face and identity the same. The result is a 16:9 image with large, high-contrast text and one clear subject that still reads on a phone screen.
The layout leaves the bottom-right corner free of text and faces. YouTube places the video length badge there, and anything underneath it is hidden.
You download a 1280×720 px JPG under 2 MB, which also fits YouTube's mobile upload limit, and a 1920×1080 px version for a sharper source image.

whatYouGet.title: 1280×720 px JPG under 2 MB
whatYouGet.description: A standard 16:9 thumbnail that stays below the 2 MB cap YouTube applies to mobile uploads.

whatYouGet.title: 1920×1080 px Full HD copy
whatYouGet.description: A larger version when you want more resolution for desktop uploads or for reuse elsewhere.

whatYouGet.title: Headline text built in
whatYouGet.description: Up to 40 characters of bold, legible text, placed in the left or right third with strong contrast.

whatYouGet.title: Your face or product
whatYouGet.description: Upload a photo and the design puts it forward with an expressive pose, keeping the likeness.

whatYouGet.title: Ten visual styles
whatYouGet.description: From bold and high contrast to cinematic, tech review and travel, to match the tone of your channel.

useCases.title: Regular uploads
useCases.description: Make a consistent look for a weekly series by reusing the same style and a similar headline pattern.

useCases.title: Tutorials and reviews
useCases.description: Show a product or a topic clearly with a short headline that tells viewers what they will learn.

useCases.title: Vlogs and challenges
useCases.description: Put your face front and center with an expressive reaction and a headline built around the promise of the video.

useCases.title: Podcast and interview clips
useCases.description: Pair a guest's name or a bold quote with a clean background so the clip stands out in the feed.

useCases.title: Testing thumbnails
useCases.description: Generate two or three versions of the same video and swap them to see which one earns more clicks.

tips.title: Keep the headline to two to five words
tips.description: Thumbnails appear small in search and suggested videos. Short, concrete words survive; sentences do not.

tips.title: Don't repeat the title
tips.description: Let the thumbnail and the title do different jobs: the thumbnail creates curiosity, the title explains it.

tips.title: Describe the moment, not the topic
tips.description: "Me shivering but grinning in a snowy backyard ice bath" gives a stronger picture than "cold plunge video".

tips.title: Use a clear, well-lit photo of your face
tips.description: A front-facing photo with an open expression gives the best likeness. Avoid sunglasses and heavy shadows.

tips.title: Pick one focal point
tips.description: A thumbnail with one subject and one text block reads faster than a collage.

tips.title: Check it at small size
tips.description: Shrink the image to about 160 px tall. If you can still read the words and see the subject, it works.

tips.title: Be accurate
tips.description: A thumbnail should promise what the video delivers. Misleading images lose viewers and can break YouTube's rules.

styleGuide.heading: Choosing a thumbnail style
styleGuide.intro: The style sets the color, contrast and mood. Match it to the kind of video you make.

items.title: Bold & high contrast
items.description: Saturated colors and strong separation. A safe default for most channels.

items.title: Clean & minimal
items.description: Simple background and calm layout. Good for tutorials, finance and productivity.

items.title: Cinematic
items.description: Film-like lighting and depth. Good for storytelling, documentaries and trailers.

items.title: Playful cartoon
items.description: Bright, illustrated and fun. Good for kids, games and light entertainment.

items.title: Warm vlog
items.description: Soft light and friendly tones. Good for lifestyle, travel diaries and daily vlogs.

items.title: Tech review
items.description: Sleek surfaces and sharp product focus. Good for gadgets and software.

items.title: Dark & eerie
items.description: Deep shadows and tension. Good for mysteries, horror and true crime.

items.title: Retro gaming
items.description: Pixel-inspired color and arcade energy. Good for gaming channels.

items.title: Fitness & energy
items.description: Dynamic angles and intense color. Good for workouts and sports.

items.title: Travel & explore
items.description: Open landscapes and bright skies. Good for adventure and destination videos.

checklist.heading: Before you upload to YouTube Studio
items: Read the headline letter by letter and check that it matches what you typed.
Check the thumbnail at about 160 px tall to confirm the text and subject are still clear.
Confirm the bottom-right corner is empty, so the video length badge does not hide anything important.
Make sure the thumbnail honestly reflects the video.
Keep the file under 2 MB if you upload from the YouTube mobile app, or under the desktop limit shown in YouTube's help.
Verify your account in YouTube Studio if custom thumbnails are not available to you yet.
Check that the thumbnail follows YouTube's Community Guidelines, which apply to every custom thumbnail.

limits: The maker creates 16:9 thumbnails for standard videos. It does not produce the vertical 9:16 thumbnails that YouTube recommends for Shorts.
Likeness is preserved well in most cases, but not perfectly. Review faces closely before publishing.
Text is part of the image, so changing a word means generating again.
It does not add your channel logo, and it does not guarantee more views. A good thumbnail helps but the video still has to deliver.
Custom thumbnails require a verified YouTube account.
